summary: The note profiles the Silverton Community Learning Center (SCLC), established in fall 2023, as a hub for lifelong learning serving all ages. It walks through a typical day, covering art therapy, coding, ESL, youth robotics, adult culinary and business classes, music workshops, a health fair, storytelling, vocational training and digital literacy. Quotes from learners and instructors show how the center builds skills, community and cross-generational connection.
one_line: The Silverton Community Learning Center, opened in fall 2023, offers lifelong learning programs for all ages, from ESL and robotics to culinary arts and digital literacy.
key_facts: The Silverton Community Learning Center (SCLC) was established in the fall of 2023 in Silverton.
Margaret Wiley, a retired nurse, attends art therapy classes at SCLC and says it is about "expression and connection."
Akash Singh, 35, is transitioning careers and uses the SCLC computer lab for coding tutorials.
Rachel Adams, the ESL instructor, says the classes foster "a sense of community and belonging" beyond grammar and vocabulary.
High school students at SCLC take tutoring sessions to prepare for the SATs.
Ten-year-old Jamal Wright attends a robotics workshop, an after-school program supported by local engineering firms to spark interest in STEM.
Laura Wright, Jamal's mother, says Jamal is learning skills he would not otherwise encounter until high school.
Linda Martinez, 42, is enrolled in a culinary program and dreams of opening her own bakery.
Adult education at SCLC ranges from business management to culinary arts.
Local musician Carlos Rodriguez leads a songwriting workshop for teens, saying "Music is a universal language."
Elaine Thompson, a public health officer, organizes monthly health fairs at SCLC to promote preventative care.
Ray Thomas, a local author and volunteer, runs a weekly storytelling session for children in the library corner.
SCLC offers vocational training from carpentry to digital marketing.
The center's tech labs have modern equipment and software funded by grants and community partnerships.
Jim Sanders, a 67-year-old retiree, is learning social media and online banking to stay connected and independent.
